q.en:
A product development team has team members located in four different countries. A senior manager is assigned the task of recruiting a project manager to manage this project and the virtual team.
Which skill is required for a project manager to successfully manage this team?

en: Possesses strong interpersonal skills to drive high-performing virtual teams
Plans and controls every aspect of the team's deliverables to avoid surprises
Speaks several languages and has lived in different countries
Implements the organization's standards and processes for the project

x.en: Implements the organization's standards and processes for the project

q.en:
A senior project manager is working for a company that is not yet making a profit. However, the company has many innovative projects in development. Most of the project time lines have slipped, and the staff is overwhelmed.
What should the project manager do to help the company meet their financial objectives?

en: Request that upper management hire additional staff to support the projects
Ensure that all of the projects are of high quality and are delivered on time
Prioritize the projects, giving higher priority to projects that will increase profit
Make sure the project is fast tracked so that slipped time lines are recovered

x.en: Prioritize the projects, giving higher priority to projects that will increase profit

q.en:
During project execution, a global project team was using a video conferencing tool to support the daily meetings. However, during these meetings, only a few team members were actively participating. As a result, lots of misunderstandings occurred.
What should the project manager do to address this issue?

en: Book one-on-one meetings with the team members who are not speaking up during the daily meetings to get their updates
Use round-robin check-ins to facilitate the meeting, so all participants have the opportunity to speak
Check the ground rules of the meeting to review the initial agreement with the team members
Identify one team representative to speak up during the daily meeting and share the team updates

x.en: Checking the ground rules can help to ensure that everyone understands how the meetings should be conducted.

q.en:
A company has a transformation project in progress. During a planning session, several stakeholders are in constant disagreement and often use personal arguments to support their position. Team members are getting frustrated with the situation.
What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation?

en: Reinforced that higher-level management has the decision power
Asked stakeholders not to voice their opinions during the meeting
Established ground rules before the discussion had started
Invited a high-level sponsor to the meeting to reduce the level of disagreement

x.en: Established ground rules before the discussion had started

q.en:
While monitoring a project at a work site, the project manager notices that the site team's work breaks have increased by a few minutes every week.
How should the project manager approach this?

en: Dismiss some of the workers for failing to adhere to the break policy
Issue a formal written warning to all hourly workers for their break tardiness
Reduce payment to the workers due to their extended breaks
Have a meeting with the team to discuss the issue and propose solutions

x.en: Have a meeting with the team to discuss the issue and propose solutions

q.en:
After signing an agreement with a vendor, the project manager notices that the vendor is continuously asking for changes on the procurement statement of work (SOW). These changes would improve the project outcome.
What should the project manager do next?

en: Revise the procurement control process to avoid undesired changes that might affect the schedule
Assess the situation as an opportunity for improvement and perform a risk analysis
Conduct an audit on the procurement process and inform the vendor about the audit's observations
Consult the list of selected vendors for the bid and evaluate a possible change of vendor

x.en: This changes would improve the project outcome". A supplier doesn't generally have all the information for such a statement, this imply that this statement have been formulated by the someone in the project management core team. Therefore the best option (Assess the situation as an opportunity for improvement and perform a risk analysis).

q.en:
A project manager is performing earned value management (EVM) for a cross-country pipeline project. The project manager has determined the ratio of earned value (EV) to actual cost (AC) for the project and has found the calculated result to be 0.9024.
What does this value mean for the project?

en: The project has earned more value than planned
The project is close to exceeding the planned cost
The project has started exceeding the planned cost
The project is earning less value than was planned

x.en: The ratio of earned value (EV) to actual cost (AC) = 0.9024 EV , The project has earned more value than planned.

q.en:
An unforeseen event has shut down public works projects for 4 weeks. Activities on the critical path will fall behind based on the project schedule.
What should the project manager do?

en: Review the project management plan to see the impact of the possible delay
Add 4 additional weeks to the schedule and request additional resources
Crash the resource management plan to keep the schedule on track
Ask the sponsor to obtain a special work permit to continue work

x.en: The project manager should review the project management plan to assess the impact of the unexpected event on the project schedule, budget, and scope. he should analyze the project schedule to identify any critical activities that may fall behind and determine if there is any flexibility in the schedule to accommodate the delay. They should also assess the available resources and determine if additional resources are required to get the project back on track. Based on this analysis, the project manager should develop a plan to mitigate the impact of the delay on the project and communicate the plan to the stakeholders.

q.en:
During a regular project progress meeting, the CEO informed the project manager that a major stakeholder has been unaware of recent developments on the project. The project manager is sure that the stakeholder was duly identified and classified in the stakeholder register.
Which project document should the project manager review in order to determine the reason for this issue?

en: Issue log
Stakeholder engagement assessment matrix
Requirements traceability matrix
Stakeholder register

x.en: Now the project manager is trying to find our the reason for this issue. So he needs to check Stakeholder engagement assessment matrix

q.en:
A healthcare organization hired a new compliance specialist to ensure that the healthcare compliance needs are met. The feedback about the new compliance specialist from the team was average.
What should the project manager do to help the new compliance specialist improve?

en: Provide time for the specialist to adjust to the pace of the project
Escalate this situation to the manager of the area for a possible solution
Contact the human resources (HR) manager about the team's feedback
Coordinate a one-to-one meeting with the specialist to assess the situation

x.en: Coordinate a one-to-one meeting with the specialist to assess the situation

q.en:
A company that uses a predictive approach and operates in a highly regulated market is losing profitability because its product life cycle is taking longer than those of its competitors. A new project manager has been hired to change this scenario.
What approach should the project manager propose?

en: Propose a hybrid approach, leveraging the benefits of an agile approach while respecting some aspects of the company's industry
Migrate to an agile model, focusing primarily on an iterative approach, leaving the incremental life cycle as a next step
Change to an agile model, focusing primarily on the incremental life cycle, leaving the iterative approach as a next step
Maintain a predictive approach, but increase the focus on better planning and tracking to anticipate problems and avoid delays

x.en: Propose a hybrid approach, leveraging the benefits of an agile approach while respecting some aspects of the company's industry

q.en:
A project manager assigned team members to work in pairs on a large amount of technical reports. At times, the project manager noticed that important information was not shared properly among the team. This has caused delivery delays and, ultimately, the failure to complete the project.
What is the root cause of this issue?

en: Improper assignment of tasks to team member pairings
Incorrect communication techniques applied during implementation
Team cohesiveness was lost because team members worked in pairs
Lack of team member training on documentation planning

x.en: The project manager noticed that important information ((was not shared properly)) among the team so the cause of the problem communications techniques

q.en:
A software system is being built for a company. Once the system is in production, the team would like to collect usage data to evaluate the delivered value.
Which evaluation practice should the project lead use to obtain accurate usage data?

en: Build the functionality in the software to collect the operational usage data
Embed a feedback form into the system for users to respond
Send out a questionnaire to all users regarding the most useful features
Interview a sampling of users to obtain the usage data

x.en: Build the functionality in the software to collect the operational usage data

q.en:
A project manager is managing a national rollout for an innovative product in a regulated environment that is expected to change. The project management office
(PMO) needs visibility of the regulatory constraints while maintaining a degree of flexibility.
Which tool can the project manager use?

en: Use a burndown chart to provide transparency
Use a product backlog to manage changes
Use a kanban board to increase accountability
Use a burnup chart to provide transparency

x.en: The backlog is continuously updated as new requirements emerge or existing ones change. The project manager can use the product backlog to manage changes and ensure that the project team is aware of the regulatory constraints. By keeping the product backlog updated, the project manager can maintain flexibility and adjust the project's scope to accommodate regulatory changes.

q.en:
A project manager for a factory construction project in a small town is evaluating the necessary actions to engage stakeholders. The local community is speculating the impact of the facility. There are rumors of job opportunities and environmental impacts, which are listed on the project risk matrix.
What should the project manager do with regard to community engagement in this situation?

en: Build channels to extend communication efforts to the local community
Focus on the sideward stakeholders only and let the organization manage the community
Use the city administration to address communication with the community
Include the local union representative in the high-power, high-impact stakeholder group

x.en: The project manager should identify all stakeholders, including the local community, and build communication channels to provide accurate information about the project's objectives, timelines, and potential impact. By doing so, the project manager can address any concerns the local community may have and manage their expectations.

q.en:
A company has rolled out the latest retail management system, and the project has been handed over to operations. The operations team finds that many of the day-to-day requirements are not covered in the system, and support for the project has limited hours. The project team has dissolved and the contract resources are no longer working on the project. As a result, the operations team has been facing numerous customer issues.
What should the project lead have done initially to avoid this situation?

en: Reviewed the project management plan
Created a detailed operations manual
Involved operations stakeholders during planning
Increased support hours for the hours of operation

x.en: Involved operations stakeholders during planning

q.en:
A project team is transitioning from a predictive to an agile approach. The project manager is trying to minimize the support issues that the product has had in production. One particular pain point is the transition to operations, where the issues usually arise.
What should the project manager do to improve this scenario?

en: Increase the focus on backlog items that cover support requirements, as well as product manuals and operation guides
Ask the support/operation team to participate in the daily standup meetings to contribute to the project's progress
Foster stakeholder participation by engaging them early on the backlog discussions
Engage the operation teams in the retrospectives and demo sessions and incorporate their feedback on project activities

x.en: The Operations team is not involved in a spint retrospective. It is with the development team to look at what went well, what did not, and what could be done better.

q.en:
A project manager has been assigned a project to build a new solar farm that will provide clean energy to a new housing complex. The government has decided to reduce the tax on renewable energy products starting 1 January. The supplier has reached out and stated that the order placed for solar panels to be delivered on
20 December might be delayed until early January. On the other hand, the project will face similar constraints due to the December holidays.
What should the project manager do about this risk?

en: Insist that the supplier deliver the goods on the agreed date
Review the supplier's contract to understand the terms of sale
Accept the risk and update the risk register
Update the risk register and take advantage of the opportunity

x.en: It is positive risk that should be exploited

q.en:
A project manager is assigned to manage a project for a previous client of the company. The project manager was warned that this client will likely try to add extra scope to the project without considering the impact of change on time, cost, quality, and risks.
Which action should the project manager take to help plan and manage the budget and resources?

en: Decompose the deliverables into work packages and review the project charter
Create tight scope statements and review the historical information
Refuse to allow the client to change the scope and examine the lessons learned register
Include a scope change process and review the project charter

x.en: The project manager should include a scope change process that outlines the steps for requesting, evaluating, approving, and managing scope changes. This process should be communicated to the client and the project team to ensure everyone understands how changes will be managed. The project manager should also review the project charter, which outlines the project's goals, objectives, and scope. This will help ensure that any proposed scope changes are aligned with the project's objectives and goals.

q.en:
A project manager is managing a project with a hybrid approach and has requested a senior team member to perform a quantitative risk analysis. The team member responds that they do not have the knowledge to perform such an analysis.
What should the project manager do?

en: Contact the project management office (PMO) and request them to assign another team member who has the knowledge to perform this task to the team
Escalate the issue to the functional manager
Perform the quantitative risk analysis for the team member
Help the team member to perform the quantitative risk analysis through coaching, mentoring, and training

x.en: Help the team member to perform the quantitative risk analysis through coaching, mentoring, and training

q.en:
A senior developer working on a large artificial intelligence (AI) project has worked hard and shown excellent results. The project manager is very happy with the developer's contribution and thinks that the developer deserves a reward.
What should the project manager do?

en: Reward the developer according to their motivations and interests
Print a recognition certificate and present it to the developer during a meeting
Send a recognition email to the team and copy management
Create an opportunity for the project team to recognize this developer

x.en: Reward the developer according to their motivations and interests

q.en:
A global program is being kicked off, and various distributed teams are involved in delivering the initiative. Besides planning and executing the scope for the initiative, team interactions must be considered.
How should the project teams interact in their meetings?

en: Phone conversations
Chat conversations
Encrypted emails
Videoconferencing

x.en:
Videoconferencing

A method enables the project teams interact in their meetings when they are distributed in different location or in global project

q.en:
A project manager is part of a global project team and is in charge of managing the scope defined by their country. There is a clear division regarding which pieces of the scope should be treated by global and local teams. During the last sprints, the project manager has been receiving requests that the global team should handle.
What should the project manager do in this situation?

en: Escalate the situation to the project sponsor
Assess the team's capacity to absorb the workload
Reject the workload back to the global team
Evaluate and understand the cause of the conflict

x.en: There is a clear conflict or "division regarding which pieces of the scope should be treated by global and local teams."

q.en:
A company is transitioning projects from a predictive to an agile approach. The CFO is concerned that one of the agile projects has an important feature for the financial department that is being delayed for a later iteration.
What should the project manager do to clarify the situation?

en: Request support from the CEO on how to deal with the situation
Clarify with the CFO that the prioritization process is based on business value
Create an executive board to review the product backlog and replan the next iterations
Increase the size of the team in order to match any prior expectations of the CFO

x.en: Clarify with the CFO that the prioritization process is based on business value

q.en:
A project manager for a technologically complex engagement reviews the key project indicators with the main stakeholders on a regular basis. During one of the meetings, the project sponsor explains that they are using the project manager's risk register as a way to communicate about the project at the executive level.
How should the project manager ensure that project risks are reported accurately in the risk register?

en: Review the risks throughout project execution
List the project risks identified in the kick-off meeting
Update the risks in the risk management plan
Plan to update the risks at project closure

x.en: Review the risks throughout project execution

q.en:
A project manager recently finished a project and started managing a new project with a different supervisor. As part of the early project activities, the supervisor from the original project is assigned to the team as a nonsupervisory resource and immediately begins challenging all decisions made by the current supervisor.
What should the project manager do to resolve this conflict?

en: Immediately remove the resource from the project team
Communicate with the resource on the roles and responsibilities of this project
Give the project team time to work through the issues with the new supervisor
Ensure the new supervisor takes the lead when being challenged

x.en: Communicate with the resource on the roles and responsibilities of this project

q.en:
A project manager sent the first communication about the project management plan to the team. The next day, two field engineers were asking about their roles and the project schedule.
What should the project manager have done?

en: Sent the roles and responsibilities matrix along with the project management plan
Confirmed that the communication was understood and solicited feedback from the team
Discussed the roles with the managers to help explain them to their team members
Briefed each team member on their roles before sending the project management plan

x.en: Since the project management plan includes roles and schedule. Also, only two members ask that questions, which means the communication is not clear for these two members.

q.en:
A project manager is managing a project that is halfway through its execution phase, and the quality standards of the deliverables were formally accepted.
However, a government agency has recently introduced new standards that may significantly impact the project. The deliverables must be changed to align with the new quality standards.
What should the project manager do?

en: Evaluate the impact the new regulations will have on the project and submit a change request
Set up a structured, independent processes to determine if project activities followed the standards
Schedule training for the project team on the new regulations introduced by the government agency
Update the lessons learned register and inform senior management of the new standards

x.en: A government agency has recently introduced new standards that may significantly impact the project so the project manager should Set up a structured, independent processes to determine if project activities followed the standards

q.en:
A self-organizing team for a critical project is consistently delivering value according to their commitments. During a retrospective, the project manager observed that most of the team members were stressed due to over commitments.
What should the project manager do?

en: Support the team during the planning phase to only commit to what they are able to deliver
Request additional resources to continue delivering value while reducing team stress
Help the team members by organizing regular stress-relieving and team- building sessions
Ask individual team members to plan staggered leave to avoid becoming stressed

x.en: Stress can only be taken away from you if you commit to what you are able to deliver." Working in Sprints at a sustainable pace improves the Scrum Team’s focus and consistency."

q.en:
A project manager received the project charter for a new product. The project is expected to have two main deliveries: the hardware part that has detailed specifications already defined, including a sample machine, and the user interface software that has only a basic specification and a requirement for a user experience design approach.
Which project management approach should the project manager use?

en: The software development has a high uncertainty level, so an agile approach is recommended for the project.
The scope is well defined; therefore, a predictive approach is straightforward and the hardware and software can by synchronized on the gates
The deliverables are significantly different, so the project should be split into two projects that are driven by a program.
A hybrid approach will work, using agile for software development and a predictive approach for the hardware deliveries

x.en: The project manager should use A hybrid approach will work using agile for software development which has only a basic specification and a predictive approach for the hardware deliveries which has detailed specifications

q.en:
An agile team member received certification on a new tool; however, this team member is complaining that the rest of the team is not using the tool due to lack of knowledge.
How should the servant leader apply emotional intelligence to leverage this situation to benefit the project?

en: Provide an incentive to team members who begin using the new tool on this project.
Ask the team member to use their recently acquired knowledge to develop and provide training to the team
Request budget to reward the team member so others will be motivated to obtain the same certification.
Promote the team member to product owner to leverage the new knowledge with the clients

x.en: Ask the team member to use their recently acquired knowledge to develop and provide training to the team

q.en:
A project manager has been assigned to a project after the charter has been approved. While reviewing the charter with the team, the project manager finds that some major budget items, necessary for achieving the project outcome, have been missed.
What should the project manager do next?

en: Immediately discuss this with the project sponsor and request to revisit the budget to ensure its accuracy
Add the missing budget items to the risk log and present them in the next project steering committee
Reduce the quality and cost of other deliverables to allow additional budget for the items that were missed
Start the project and deal with these budget issues as they arise throughout the project life cycle

x.en: Immediately discuss this with the project sponsor and request to revisit the budget to ensure its accuracy

q.en:
A project schedule risk has turned into an issue. The project manager foresees delays in project execution.
What should the project manager do to resolve the issue?

en: Update the schedule baseline to the new project time line
Escalate the issue to senior leadership for resolution
Update the risk management plan and send it to the project team
Work with relevant stakeholders to determine possible solutions

x.en: Work with relevant stakeholders to determine possible solutions

q.en:
A project is comprised of team members who are not engaged and committed to project success.
What should the project manager do to address this situation?

en: Accept the situation knowing there is schedule slack available to release on an incremental basis when necessary
Call each team member to gain their perspective on the problem, then bring the whole team together to discuss a solution
Contact the project sponsor to request approval to release the current team and hire replacement personnel
Send each team member a direct email indicating that disciplinary action is likely if they do not change their attitude

x.en: Contact the project sponsor to request approval to release the current team and hire replacement personnel

q.en:
In a time-critical construction project, a misunderstanding occurred between the supervisor and the technician. The misunderstanding turned into a major conflict and the technician has complained to the project manager that they cannot continue to work under the supervisor any longer. The supervisor cites the technician's poor performance as the reason for the conflict.
How should the project manager resolve the problem?

en: Provide a just-in-time training to the technician to improve their skill set
Use a direct, collaborative approach with the technician and supervisor
Talk to the supervisor to tone down their approach and attitude
Replace the technician with a high performing resource as time is critical

x.en: Use a direct, collaborative approach with the technician and supervisor

q.en:
A project manager is assigned to a project where a vendor has been engaged to build a new system. One week before user acceptance testing (UAT) is scheduled, the vendor informs the project manager that they can only deliver half of the promised functions by the UAT start date.
What should the project manager do next?

en: Adjust the project schedule to accommodate the current development progress of the vendor
Communicate with the vendor and project team and explore possibilities for resolving the issue
Wait until the vendor cannot deliver and then invoke liquidated damages based on the contract
Escalate to management and prepare for project closure by canceling the contract with this vendor

x.en: Communicate with the vendor and project team and explore possibilities for resolving the issue

q.en:
A project manager has been assigned to lead a software project to generate savings at an important financial institution. Initially, the duration of the project was 13 months, but due to various issues during execution, the project was extended to 16 months. By month 11, the expected savings were exceeded but not all of the functionalities planned for that date were fulfilled.
How should the project manager inform the stakeholders of the project's progress?

en: Communicate the benefit expectations and the action plan for the pending functionalities
Send an email with the monthly project progress to all relevant stakeholders
Complete the outstanding functionalities before informing the sponsor of the project progress
Report that the project has not fulfilled all the expected functionalities

x.en: "Benefit expectations" should be reworded with "realized benefits" to make it more understandable

q.en:
A project manager is assigned to a new project that will launch the digital version of a current product. Even though the product is well known, the vision for its digital version is not clear to the stakeholders.
What should the project manager do to increase value delivery?

en: Gather the team to create a comprehensive product roadmap but only commit to requirements for the next quarter
Create a visual task board with all of the relevant stakeholders to support backlog prioritization
Work with the team on the definition of a minimum viable product (MVP) and present it to the stakeholders
Use spikes to dig deeper into the technical challenges of the new product, thus reducing the technical risk

x.en: By working with the team on the definition of a minimum viable product (MVP) and presenting it to the stakeholders, the project manager can gather feedback on the direction of the project and get buy-in from stakeholders. This approach also ensures that the team focuses on delivering the most important features first, which can reduce the risk of building unnecessary features. Once the MVP is defined, the project manager can then work with the team to break it down into smaller, manageable tasks for development.

q.en:
A team working on a close deployment waits to receive critical information from the customer. The customer keeps postponing sending the information which is delaying the deployment.
What should the project manager have done to prevent the delay?

en: Used the sample data already in place
Involved the customer in the deployment process
Involved upper management in the process
Obtained all critical information ahead of time

x.en: Identify and analyse well the stakeholders and their power / interest on the project so as to know how to better manage them. In this situation the customer has high power but low interest so needs to be actively consulted. The best way to go is to engage them in the deployment process.

q.en:
A project team is implementing a hosted system for a third party. Just before going live, the customer asks the project team to include additional functionality. The project team identified risks to the delivery date and informed the project manager that some of the requested functions are in conflict with the agreed scope.
What should the project manager do?

en: Ask the team to deliver the functionality on the agreed go-live date
Discuss with the customer the risks identified and team's concerns
Ask the customer to go live and add the new functionality in the backlog
Discuss with the team, estimate the effort, and raise a change request

x.en: The risk has already been identified, evaluated by the project team and its impact already determined as to have conflit with the scope. The next thing to do is to inform the customer and discuss raised concerns with him on the impact this change will have on the scope.

q.en:
A project manager identifies an issue between two team members that is affecting the development of one of the deliverables during the second iteration of a project.
How should the project manager address this issue to avoid any impact to the project?

en: Escalate both team members to their respective functional managers and let them take the appropriate actions
Schedule a meeting with both team members to understand the issue and facilitate a solution that satisfies both parties
Send a warning to both team members indicating that if the issue continues, both will be removed from the project
Contact the functional managers to request substitutes for the conflicting team members

x.en: Schedule a meeting with both team members to understand the issue and facilitate a solution that satisfies both parties

q.en:
During the execution of a project, a company decides that everybody will need to take vacation time before the end of the year. This may cause a change in the project time line.
How should the project manager address the situation?

en: Agree with functional management and team members on a vacation schedule that would minimally impact the project schedule
Discuss the vacation plan and include scheduling changes in the change log database
Push out the project timeline according to the vacation plan in place based on the recent company policy
Submit a formal request to senior management asking them not to proceed with this decision based on the impact it will have on the project

x.en: Notice it didn't say all workers will go on vacation the same day or period. It simply says before the year ends. The project manager in the Schedule Management during the Develope Schedule Process considers as an input the Resource Managment Plan during Aquire/allocate Resource Process developed with the help of the functional manager incharge of the resources and which usually takes into consideration such scenarios. The Vacation plan is thus discused and shedule replanned accordingly. Normally this is achieved through lags placed on activities.

q.en:
A project manager wants to assign a junior engineer to a new project. In past projects, the engineer showed initiative to take on complex tasks and solve problems in innovative ways without any need for encouragement. However, the engineer declines the project manager's invitation to join the new project.
What is the most likely reason for the engineer's refusal to work on the project?

en: The project manager did not follow the normal hiring process with the engineer's functional manager
The project manager did not sufficiently support and recognize the engineer's professional growth
The engineer has "project burnout" from working long hours and solving difficult problems
The engineer did not feel welcome or enjoy working with the other project team members

x.en: Based on this phrase in the question "showed initiative to take on complex tasks and solve problems in innovative ways without any need for encouragement" gives an impression that he would not decline a request to tackle a project of interest simply because he wasn't supported with training and development.

q.en:
Eight highly qualified experts have been assembled to work for a 6-month period on a specific aspect of an organization's product development process.
How should the project manager support this team to succeed?

en: Define roles and targets for all team members and regularly follow up with one-to-one meetings to review progress
Work with the team members to define the overall objective and support them to engage around the goal
Hand over control of specific aspects of their roles as experts and let them agree on their own timelines and targets
Bring in a senior colleague who is also an expert to ensure the team is on track to achieve the goals and objectives

x.en: The project manager is a servant leader that should act like a facilitator to the highly qualified team members in establishing a safe, trustworthy and transparent working environement while communioning them to a common project goal

q.en:
A controller proposed a budget reduction for projects because the majority of implemented solutions resulted in little returns on investment (ROI) or operational improvements. The project manager objected and presented project assets showing all solutions having been demonstrated, accepted, and delivered within the relevant framework constraints. The project manager suggested that the issues may stem from the project evaluation and selection processes.
What was the project manager demonstrating?

en: Strategic negotiation techniques in determining budget priorities in future sessions
Risk management in addressing impediments, obstacles, and blockers to project success
Cause-and-effect identification in root cause analysis toward achieving project value
Multiple stages of development that members may go through toward working formation

x.en: The project manager was demonstrating a focus on the project evaluation and selection processes, suggesting that the issues with low ROI or operational improvements may have been caused by flaws in the decision-making process rather than the solutions themselves. The project manager is attempting to identify the root cause of the problem to address it properly and improve the overall effectiveness of future project evaluation and selection

q.en:
A new law was published about zoning permits for telecom towers. This may cause cost and schedule overruns for the new network rollout.
What should the project manager do?

en: Update the project plan because the law is an obligation for the project
Meet the sponsor to ask for additional time and budget increase
Minimize the scope to catch the cost and schedule baseline
Assess and prioritize the impact of the new law on the project plan

x.en: Assess and prioritize the impact of the new law on the project plan

q.en:
A project manager is evaluating a project and realizes that its earned value (EV) shows the cost spent is higher than the value delivered. The project manager then discovers that the team has been adding small features that are not part of the requirements.
What should the project manager do?

en: Encourage the team to continue, as this will eventually help the customer
Request additional budget because additional features are being added
Ask the product owner to add the additional features to the requirements
Ask the team to focus on and deliver only the agreed-upon features

x.en: The best option (Ask the team to focus on and deliver only the agreed-upon features)The reason is that the team is adding scope creep, which is adding features that are not part of the original requirements or scope baseline. This causes the actual cost (AC) to be higher than the earned value (EV), which means the project is over budget. The project manager should control the scope and ensure that only the features that are approved by the change control board (CCB) are implemented. Requesting additional budget or asking the product owner to add the features to the requirements are not good practices, as they do not follow the change management process. Encouraging the team to continue may not satisfy the customer or stakeholders, as they may not need or want the extra features.

q.en:
A project's customer is furious. When the customer arrived at the project site, they discovered that one of their requirements was not met.
What should the project manager do?

en: Consult the scope management plan with the customer to understand the gap
Discuss and agree with the customer to implement the missing requirement
Refer to the requirements traceability matrix and analyze the requirement
Analyze the benefits management plan and implement the needed change

x.en: Requirement not met means it was already defined in planning during Define Requirement Process before Create Scope Statement Process. A requirment traceability matrix should be consulted to have more information on this requirment and how it is linked to other artifacts of the project.

q.en:
A project manager is managing an internal project that was poorly defined. Recently, the project manager received several change requests raised by the organization's upper management.
What should the project manager do first?

en: Motivate the team to avoid the frustration of working on a prolonged project
Assess the time overrun, and start implementation to avoid additional delays
Request a provisional budget increase to avoid any budget overruns
Review the benefits of the proposed changes in relation to the business case

x.en: First the project manager should Review the benefits of the proposed changes in relation to the business case

q.en:
A state-of-the-art product was delivered at the end of a project life cycle. However, the customer claims the product was not designed to specifications.
What should the project manager have done to avoid this issue?

en: The customer's requirements should have been captured in order to meet the customer's standards.
The customer's requirements should have been captured and modified to meet the supplier's standards.
The sprint retrospective meeting should have included necessary stakeholders
The iteration review planning meeting should have been planned accordingly

x.en:
Its a predictive scenario. The Scope Management with its respective processes of Collect Requirements Process and Validate Scope Process would have handled this.
Delivery at the end of a project lifecycle and not at the end of an iteration means predictive. If it was Agile, the issue would've been addressed at one of the Iteration review sessions.

q.en:
A project manager has been asked for performance feedback regarding one of the team members. The project manager would like to gather additional input from the project team because there are no metrics in place for evaluating employee performance.
What should the project manager do next?

en: Analyze team member influence
Identify levels of decision-making authority
Determine the appropriate approach
Evaluate demonstrated task accountability

x.en:
Determine the appropriate approach.
The project manager should first determine the appropriate approach to gather feedback from the project team. There are different methods that can be used such as one-on-one meetings, surveys, or group discussions. The appropriate approach will depend on factors such as the size of the team, the nature of the project, and the culture of the organization.

Once the appropriate approach has been determined, the project manager can proceed to gather feedback from the team members. The feedback should focus on the team member's performance in relation to their assigned tasks, their ability to work collaboratively with others, and any other relevant factors that contribute to their performance on the project.

q.en:
A new major road project is starting, and the contractor has contractually committed to submitting regular status reports and participating in integration meetings.
Halfway through the project life cycle, the contractor stops participating in meetings and submitting reports, stating these items consume too much time.
What should the project manager do first?

en: Remind the contractor that they committed to attending meetings and submitting reports per the contract
Submit a claim for not fulfilling the contract terms and handle the claim in accordance with the alternative dispute resolution
Speak with the company's lawyer and request that they demand the contractor fulfill their contractual commitments
Assess the risk of the contractor not attending meetings and submitting reports for the rest of the project and escalate it to the project sponsor

x.en:
Key word is what should Project Manager do first.?
 First thing is to remind the contractor

q.en:
While finalizing project management plans, a customer provides the project manager with a new set of quality standards to which the final product must adhere.
What should the project manager do to ensure a smooth delivery of the product?

en: Agree with the client on a new project charter
Involve the client in a performance gap analysis
Involve the client in risk identification
Agree with the client on acceptance criteria

x.en: When a customer provides a project manager with a new set of quality standards, the project manager should work with the customer to establish clear acceptance criteria that meet the new standards. The acceptance criteria should be measurable and should outline specific objectives that the final product must meet to be considered acceptable. By agreeing with the client on acceptance criteria, the project manager can ensure that the final product meets the customer's expectations and the new quality standards. This will help to prevent any misunderstandings or disagreements about the quality of the final product and ensure a smooth delivery of the product.

q.en:
A project manager has been given a critical, 5-day window and is allocated a maximum of US$100,000 as a contingency reserve. Subsequently, the project manager drafted a course of action based upon the best available information. Overall, five actions were required to be completed at a cost of US$20,000 and a duration of 1 day each. After 3 days of work, the project manager completed two actions and spent US$80,000.
What should the project manager do next?

en: Complete all actions and then inform the client of the additional cost and schedule overrun needed to complete the project
As the cost performance index (CPI) and schedule performance index (SPI) are less than 1.0, reevaluate and prioritize the remaining actions
Stop the work and raise a project change request to the change control board (CCB) for additional funds and a project schedule extension
As the CPI and SPI are greater than 1.0, reevaluate and prioritize the remaining actions

x.en:
CPI = Earned Value (EV) / Actual Value (AC)
EV = The progress X Budgeted Cost = 2 (actions completed) X 20,000 (cost of each action) =40,000
AC = Actual amount spent after two actions = 80,000
Therefore, CPI = 40000 / 80000 =0.5
Now, When the CPI < 1.0, then your project is over-costed or over-budgeted.
You have to re-evaluate and prioritize the remaining actions so that you are within the planned budget

q.en:
A project manager wants to make sure that similar projects in the future use the project's performance data as a reference. However, the project manager is not sure how to accomplish this.
What should the project manager do?

en: Send periodic emails to senior management with the latest project updates
Keep project artifacts up-to-date and accessible to all stakeholders
Share project documentation in a repository with exclusive access
Schedule weekly knowledge-sharing sessions with key stakeholders

x.en:
Project artifacts are the documentation and other tangible outputs of the project, such as plans, schedules, status reports, and lessons learned. These artifacts are important sources of information that can be used to improve the management of future projects. Keeping project artifacts up-to-date and accessible to all stakeholders will help ensure that future projects can benefit from the performance data of the current project.
 
 Lessons learned are updated through out the project and final update done at the end of the project and archived. This will be a repository (DB) for future projects which will provide valuable information to the future PMs and othe stakeholders when considerations to take when carrying future similar projects

Option(Sharing project documentation in a repository with exclusive access), may limit the accessibility of the information and exclude stakeholders who could benefit from it.

q.en:
A project is 70% complete when the project sponsor requests an additional deliverable.

What should the project manager do first?

en: Negotiate with the project sponsor on the possible alternatives
Reject the request as being too late and leading to major scope creep
Submit the request to the change control board (CCB) for a decision
Determine the possible impact of this change on all aspects of the project

x.en: First , the project manager should Determine the possible impact of this change on all aspects of the project then Submit the request to the change control board (CCB) for a decision

q.en:
A company initiated a departmental transformation project improving the processes for the organization using a predictive approach. This is a critical project for the organization and, in the middle of the project, the project manager noticed that one of the deliverables cannot be produced due to a missing technical skill.
What should the project manager have done to avoid this?

en: Identified all required skills after the kick-off of the project
Planned all required training for the team during the onboarding process
Identified all required skills during the planning of the project
Asked the sponsor to identify all required skills during the planning of the project

x.en:
The keyword of this question is "What should the Project Manager have done", what should the Project Manager do in the first place, not what should the Project Manager do right now
This should have been handled in the planning phase of Resource Management during the Estimate Resource Process.
Project Manager is meant to hire ready skills, there is no time for training in a project. Therefore he should have planned for this earlier.

q.en:
A project manager is beginning a new project with very diverse team members. The project manager chose to use consensus building so the team can agree on and be engaged in how the project will be executed.
How should the project manager proceed?

en: Create an environment where the agreement is reached through discussion
Establish recurring brainstorming sessions to discuss project issues
Allow team members to contribute ideas in a stream-of-consciousness mode
Create an environment where the agreement is reached by a majority vote

x.en:
Create an environment where the agreement is reached through discussion.

Consensus building involves creating an environment where team members can discuss and agree on the execution of the project. The project manager should encourage open communication and active listening among team members to ensure that everyone's ideas and concerns are heard and addressed.

Consensus building is based on the principles of local participation and ownership of decisions. Ideally, the consensus reached will meet all of the relevant interests of stakeholders, who thereby come to a unanimous agreement.

q.en:
A project manager is leading a team of diverse individuals of all ages. The working hours for the project were set at the beginning of the project, and all team members agreed to the hours. However, later in the project, one of the team members informed the project manager that the previously agreed upon hours no longer work due to the team member's personal commitments.
What should the project manager do?

en: Remove the team member from the project team to be fair to the other members
Discuss the lack of dedication with the team member and their functional manager
Allow the most senior team members to decide the time that works for the team
Reassess the team's hours collaboratively so that the team is not impeded by the issue

x.en: Reassess the team's hours collaboratively so that the team is not impeded by the issue

q.en:
A company is implementing a growth strategy by constructing a new production facility, which will soon move into the operation phase. Although a governance policy was already in place, the company must comply with new financial regulations that have been recently implemented. Compliance with the regulations will cause a major change in project scope.
How should the project manager respond to this requirement?

en: Escalate the issue to upper management and let them decide
Perform an analysis to assess the Impact on the project
Directly comply with the financial regulations
Proceed with the existing company governance policy

x.en: First thing is impact analysis .

q.en:
A project manager has been assigned to an emergency project that must be completed within the next few weeks. The project manager realizes this will have an impact on the local community. As the work is near a school, the project manager has engaged with them to understand their needs.
How should the project manager ensure the work continues smoothly?

en: Advise the school to close for the duration of the project work
Liaise with the school to include nonworking project hours during school start and finish times
Postpone the required work on the project until school holidays begin
Continue the work as planned and inform the school when the project team arrives on-site

x.en: Liaise with the school to include nonworking project hours during school start and finish times

q.en:
It is late at night on a weekend when a team member calls the project manager on the telephone. The team member is crying about the pressures of an upcoming deadline.
What should the project manager do?

en: Review the organization's human resources (HR) policy
Empathize with the team member and discuss next steps.
Ask the team member to send their concerns in writing
Schedule a meeting with the team member for the next work day

x.en:
The project manager should provide a listening ear and offer support to the team member who is under pressure and feeling overwhelmed by the upcoming deadline. The project manager should show empathy and understanding towards the team member's situation and offer words of encouragement and reassurance. This can help the team member feel heard and supported, which in turn can boost their morale and motivation.

Additionally, the project manager can discuss possible solutions or next steps with the team member, such as seeking help from other team members or reorganizing the workload. By addressing the problem and offering support, the project manager can help the team member regain a sense of control and feel more confident in meeting the deadline.

q.en:
A project manager is working with the team to deliver a project in a company that uses different delivery methods. The project manager is concerned about the communication channels currently suggested by the project management office (PMO) because some information is taking too much time to reach the team members, causing negative consequences for delivery.
How should the project manager avoid this situation in the future?

en: Tell the sponsor that the project manager will use their own communication model to ensure on-time delivery
Refer to the policies and frameworks used at the company enterprise level and inform the project team members
Agree with the project team on a suitable collaboration and make sure information is shared at all times
Use the same methods until the end of the current delivery and suggest new ones during the retrospective

x.en: Agree with the project team on a suitable collaboration and make sure information is shared at all times

q.en:
A company must implement a new regulation. The government has specified the date when the regulation will be enforced but has only provided high-level information on the regulation's requirements. Therefore, changes in definitions are to be expected due to uncertainty.
Which life cycle should the project manager use for this project?

en: An iterative execution strategy
A predictive execution strategy
An agile execution strategy
A hybrid execution strategy

x.en: There is a already a date specified to enforce the regulation and also because the regulation requirements are only known at a very high level and government and they tend to be more waterfall type, but with the new unclear requirement, they can implement more agile up to a certain point. Second, since there is some guidance out there, prefer to be hybrid.

q.en:
A project manager is managing a project that has a new sponsor who is cutting the budget.
As a servant leader, how should the project manager handle the budget cuts with the team?

en: Inform each team member that they must release a portion of their budget but must remain on schedule with no change to the scope
Meet with the schedule coordinator and financial analyst to tell them which budget lines to reduce and where to release slack
Collaborate with the team to assess the impact of the change on the project and recommend an updated project plan
Notify the project sponsor that the budget reduction will require a schedule slip and scope reduction.

x.en: Collaborate with the team to assess the impact of the change on the project and recommend an updated project plan

q.en:
A project manager has completed an assessment of the project team's performance. Some team members have performed poorly on their assigned tasks.
What should the project manager do?

en: Develop different approaches based on team members' motivation and ability
Create a new standard performance measure based on project requirements
Provide intensive oversight to the team members who performed poorly
Develop a standard approach to provide feedback to all team members

x.en: It seems the initial approaches didn't work for all, thus different approaches should be undertaken accordingly

q.en:
A project manager is leading a multiyear project that involves internal and external stakeholders. As the project manager begins to gather requirements, additional business stakeholders express interest in being involved.
Which three actions should the project manager take to ensure proper stakeholder involvement? (Choose three.)

en: Include all stakeholders in the stakeholder engagement plan and provide the same level of communication
Develop a stakeholder impact/influence matrix to determine the level of engagement
Perform a stakeholder assessment to align with the project objectives
Classify and rank stakeholders based on their positions in the organization
Prioritize stakeholders based on the project phase and need

x.en:
The three actions should the project manager take to ensure proper stakeholder involvement

1. Prioritize stakeholders based on the project phase and need.

2. Perform a stakeholder assessment to align with the project objectives.

3. Develop a stakeholder impact/influence matrix to determine the level of engagement.

q.en:
A project manager is overseeing a project as part of a program geared toward a major technology disruption. The team is comprised of brilliant young professionals who have worked on different projects for the organization in the past. However, the team complained that they previously experienced a lack of direction during project execution and are afraid of the same issue in this project.
 

Which two actions should the project manager take to ensure that this issue does not occur in this project? (Choose two.)

en: Keep the team engaged and focused on the project's direction
Focus on the resource management plan and track project progress
Organize a team-bonding activity and invite an external manager to speak to the team
Set a clear vision for the project and ensure it is visible to all stakeholders
Encourage the team to do a brainstorming session and provide a mitigation plan

x.en:
The two actions should the project manager take to ensure that this issue does not occur in this project

1. Set a clear vision for the project and ensure it is visible to all stakeholders.

2. Keep the team engaged and focused on the project's direction.

q.en:
Due to organizational changes, several key stakeholders are replaced by new ones in the middle of a project. As a result, numerous new requirements are raised.
What should the project manager do to ensure success of the project?

en: Review and prioritize new requirements with stakeholders to determine which change requests are needed.
Escalate the issue to the project sponsor and seek support to keep the original requirements
Seek immediate approval to amend the project timeline and budget in order to deliver all new requirements
Emphasize to the new stakeholders that new requirements are not allowed at this stage of the project

x.en: Need a change request, first to amend the existing requirements and accept the new requirements.

q.en: A project manager wants to ensure sufficient stakeholder participation throughout a project's life cycle . What should the project manager include in the stakeholder engagement plan?

en: Feedback from stakeholders on project operations
Stakeholder power/ interest grid
Change requests initiated by stakeholders
Desired and current stakeholder engagement levels

x.en: A model which a project manager uses to judge stakeholders’ current level of engagement with a project and the desired engagement level of each stakeholder engagement assessment matrix : stakeholder or stakeholder group. and it supports the comparison between the current engagement levels of stakeholders and the desired engagement levels required for successful project delivery.

q.en: One developer's productivity is lacking compared with the other due to repetitive attendance issue . What should the project manager do to determine the appropriate disciplinary actions specific to this project?

en: Check the resource management plan
Review the organizational process assets
Review RACI chart
Review the stakeholder register

x.en: The resource management plan provides guidance on various aspects of team development including disciplinary actions as a result of team performance assessments.

q.en: You are a project manager on a software project. You work with a global virtual team.The team is facing diffculty in communicating with each other and often misses important message . This difficulty leads to missed deadlines . What should you do to enhance project team effectiveness?

en: Initiate daily communication of project progress
Implement team colocation to improve communication
Identify the root cause of communication issues
Schedule a communication control board meeting

x.en: the root cause of the communication issue is known because you are working with a global virtual team and the team is located in different places . To enhance project team effectiveness , you should implement team colocation to improve communication.

q.en: A project manager is assigned to a project in a company that is transitioning from a traditional approach to agile . The relevant organizational personnel lacks experience with agile methodologies . The organization has elected to use hybrid life cycles as a tranisition strategy . What else should be done to facilitate the transition?

en: Eliminate the project manager's role entirely as agile teams are self- managing
Contract an external agile coach to assist the organization with the transition
Replace the existing project manager with an experienced external agile coach
Establish a directive project management office (PMO) to lead the transition

x.en: An external agile coach can bring significant experience on agile best practices to assist the project team with the transition until internal resource are able to take over the responsibility.

q.en: A new project manager has just replaced a project manager who was managing a city street light installation project. The project is in its execution phase. During the first risk review meeting , the new project manager notices that the version of the risk register used by the project team members is different from the one the project manager is using . What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation?

en: Ask help from subject matter experts
Validated the issue log
Referred to the communication management plan
Validated the project artifacts

q.en: A project manager finds an unexpected issue halfway through a customer's project. After analysis , the project team determines that the issue will affect the timeline unless more resources are allocated to the project. What should the project manager do ?

en: Inform the customer of the issue and discuss the options so that they are able to make a decision on cost versus timeline
Adjust the timeline since , in the past , the customer would not pay any additional costs , then inform the customer of the change
Absorb the additional cost for the additional resources internally so that the project completes within the timeline.
Meet with the project team to discuss internally whether they think cost is more important to the customer that the timeline

x.en: Keyword ( an unexpected issue) so the best option (nform the customer of the issue and discuss the options so that they are able to make a decision on cost versus timeline)

q.en: A project manager receives an email from a customer saying that they do not want to keep working with one of the project team members. The customer does not provide any reasons for this sentiment. The project manager is concerned because this project team member is highly skilled and experienced and is key in one of the main project deliverables. What should the project manager do to ease the situation?

en: Ask the project team member to call the customer to apologize for their behavior
Remove the project team member immediately and assign the pending activities to other team members
Tell the customer that they do not have the authority to remove project team members
Talk to the customer and project team member separately to assess the issue and decide on the next steps

x.en: If there is problem and can't know the reasons you should discuss face to face with the problem with the person who have the problem to know the reasons then develop solution so the best option (Talk to the customer and project team member separately to assess the issue and decide on the next steps)

q.en: A project manager has recently moved to an organization to lead a key project. The project manager notices that team performance is below the target , and the tasks assigned are not delivered on time . Team commitment is also not as appropriate as it should be. What should the project manager do ?

en: Study and determine the appropriate leadership style suitable for the team
Apply an agile approach to help improve team performance
Hire a project team leader who can influence the project team members
Schedule a meeting and communicate the performance concern to the team

x.en: The project manager should Study and determine the approptiate leadership style suitable for the team to improve the team performance and acheiving the target.

q.en: A project manager is leading a hybrid project. The work breakdown structure (WBS) and the schedule were developed, but the project manager is having difficulty assigning specific resources to all of the project tasks . What should the project manager do?

en: Escalate the issue to the project sponsor and seek their immediate intervention
Assign the unallocated tasks to the functional role and then reallocate when the resources are available
Ignore the unallocated tasks for now and reallocate when the resources are available
Assign the unallocated tasks to the project management office (PMO) manager and reallocate when the resources are available .

x.en: Assign the unallocated tasks to the functional role and then reallocate when the resources are available

q.en: A project stakeholder has left the company. The new stakeholder is a family member of one of the team members. This stakeholder does not attend meetings. The project manager finds out that the stakeholder has been asking the family member for project updates. What should the project manager do ?

en: Escalate this to the project sponsor
Request a meeting with the stakeholder
Forward the project status reports
Design an updated status report

x.en: You, as a project manager, should have communication skills and communicate with others. So , the project manager should meet with the stakeholder to find out the reasons for the stakeholder not attending the meetings. Escalation should not be made unless it is outside the control of the project manager. Status reports cannot be sent before the stakeholder attends the meetings.

q.en: A project manager is managing the transition to operations. The project sponsor wants to ensure that good suport is provided to the end users. What should the project manager do ?

en: Ensure that comprehensive documentation is handed over
Ensure that the user guide is detailed and has clear instructions
Ensure that knowledge is transferred to the operations team
Ask the project team to provide operational support for 1 year

q.en: A project manager is working on a complex project with a high degree of change . What strategy should the project manager use to ensure successful project completion?

en: Schedule a regular risk review with the project management team
Create a project change roadmap to keep track of all unforeseen changes
Update the project management plan to reduce the possibility of scope creep
Increase the active engagement and participation of key stakeholders

x.en:
The strategy which is fit with a complex project with a high degree of change is Increase the active engagement and participation of key stakeholders to ensure successful project completion.
As actively engaged Stakeholders may be able to provide feedback and necessary input during changes to have them incorporated smoothly. Moreover, sometimes during active communications, some risks may be revealed before they even turn into issues.

q.en: A project team is working on a risk response strategy by evaluating every risk and coming up with suitable response strategies. However , one particular risk with a negative impact cannot be avoided or mitigated. Furthermore , there is no way to tras=nsfer risk by outsourcincing or buying insurance. What is the best the team can do about the risk?

en: Share the risk by allocating ownership to a third party
Treat it as a secondary risk and update it in the risk register.
Accept the risk
Revisit the risk response strategy.

x.en: The question suggests that the team has already explored all the alternatives. In this case, the best strategy is to acceot the risk and , if possible, plan for a contingency to be implemented if risk occurs so the best option is accept the risk.

q.en: A company has recurring quality issues with one of its sole source suppliers. A new project will incur significant penalties from the customer if deliverables are late what should the project manager do ?

en: Negotiate with other vendors with better quality -control methods.
Escalate the issue to top management
Identify high -level risks prior to developing contingency plans
Review incoming inspection reports and quality logs

x.en: In the past projects , the company has recurring quality issues with ine of its sole source suppliers. in the (new project will incur significant penalties from the customer if deliverables are late . So this is high level risk and should be initially take into consideration , then in the planning phase , the project manager should conduct a mitigation plan to reduce this risk such as conduct more tests and review incoming inspection reports and quality logs. Since its sole source then you don't have any other option to negotiate with other vendors with better quality - control methods. Therefor you have to consider this risk while you are planning the project. Since you should be proactive so the escalation process to top management is the last decision.

q.en: A key stakeholder who is highly involved in the project claims that the reports sent by the project team are indequate. What should the project manager do first?

en: Ask the project team to review and modify all of these reports
Ensure that the reports comply with the communication management plan
Ask the sponsor to meet with the stakeholder to diffuse the situation with the reports
Explain to the stakeholder that these are the approved templates for the reports

x.en: A key stakeholder claims that the reports sent by the project team are indequate so the project manager should Ensure that the reports comply with the communication management plan

q.en: A project manager is well-informed on the industry standards of the organization and believes that they are not reflected in the project deliverables. What should the project manager review next?

en: Project Charter
Quality Process
Quality Management Plan
Organizational Process Assets (OPAs)

x.en: Organizational Process Asset (OPA) refers to all the implicit input or assets on processes used by an organization in operating their business. This may include business plans, processes, policies, protocols, and knowledge. While Enterprise Environmental Factors may be branched into two categories, internal and external to the organization, organization process asset is internal to the organization. It may come from the projects, programs, portfolios, documentation, or any other records in a said organization. There are three categories of organization process asset; 1) Processes, Policies, and Procedures; 2) Corporate Knowledge Base; 3) Team and SME Knowledge.

q.en: A company's key product is evolving and requires the use of new technology. No one on the team is familiar with this technology; however, experienced developers on the team volunteered to study the concepts and application and believe they will be able to take full responsibility for the new technology. What should the project manager do?

en: Support the developers with their intention to learn the new technology
Outsource the technology work to a third party so as not to delay work
De scope this requirements as the developers have more important tasks
Hire externally since the internal developers already have assigned work

x.en:
🔹 Domain: People

🔹 Approach: Agile

🔹 Importance:
Very important, because it tests your understanding of team empowerment, learning culture, and the project manager’s supportive role instead of forcing external solutions too quickly.

🔹 Keywords:
new technology – no one on the team is familiar – developers volunteered – take full responsibility

In this question, the team is facing a new technical challenge, but one very important detail is that experienced developers have shown initiative and willingness to learn and take ownership. That is a positive signal the project manager should support, not suppress or immediately replace with external resources.

In agile environments, the project manager or leader is expected to play a supportive and enabling role, helping the team grow, self-learn, and acquire new skills.
This aligns with servant leadership, where the focus is on removing impediments, providing support, and enabling team success.

Choosing external hiring or outsourcing may solve the issue faster in the short term, but it can weaken team ownership and prevent internal capability building.
De-scoping is not logical because the question clearly states that the new technology is required for the evolution of the company’s key product.

🔹 Example:
A company is enhancing a digital platform and needs to add an AI-based feature. No one on the team has enough expertise yet, but several experienced developers are willing to take quick training, study documentation, and experiment with prototypes. The best action for the project manager is to support them with training, time, coaching, and perhaps light expert guidance if needed, rather than taking the work away from them completely.

🔹 Exam Tips:
If the team shows willingness to learn or take ownership, the correct answer is often to support and empower the team.
If the question emphasizes development, empowerment, motivation, or servant leadership, avoid external contracting or imposed solutions unless clearly necessary.
If the scenario included an urgent fixed deadline or no tolerance for a learning curve, external expert support might become more appropriate, but that is not stated here.
If the wording changed to something like: The deadline is fixed and missing it will cause a regulatory violation, then outside support or a specialist might be the better answer.
In this case, the context supports internal capability building.

🔹 References:

 PMBOK 7th Edition: Pages 21–24, 33–36, 169–171
 PMBOK 6th Edition: Pages 332–337
 PMBOK 8th Edition: Pages 54–59, 118–123
 Agile Practice Guide: Pages 41–44, 56–60
 ECO 2026: Pages 6–10

q.en: A project manager is preparing to start a new project in which the team members are distributed geographically across different countries. The project manager is using the communications management plan to engage the team members and find a communication method that suits everyone. A risk register is a document used to document , analysis and track and report on project risks and opportunities throughout the project’s life cycle. q.en: A project team is conducting sprint planning. Based on the estimated effort,only 95% of the items included in the sprint may be delivered . The product owner asked the project manager for advice on how to prioritize the backlog items. What should be used to prioritize the backlog items.

en: Technical complexity
Estimation accuracy
Business Value
Risk to delivery

x.en:
🔹 Domain: Process

🔹 Approach: Agile

🔹 Importance:
Very important, because it tests how backlog items are prioritized in agile, especially when delivery capacity is limited during Sprint Planning.

🔹 Keywords:
Sprint planning – estimated effort – prioritize the backlog items

During Sprint Planning, if the team realizes that not all selected items may be delivered, the product owner should ensure that the most important items come first.
In agile, the primary basis for backlog prioritization is business value, meaning the benefit delivered to the customer or organization.

This does not mean risk, complexity, or estimates are irrelevant, but they are supporting factors rather than the primary prioritization driver.
The Product Backlog is generally ordered with highest-value items first, then effort, dependencies, risk, and feasibility are considered.

In other words:

 The product owner focuses on value
 The development team supports estimation and technical feasibility
 Prioritization should maximize delivered value

🔹 Example:
Suppose there are four features for an app, but the team can only finish three.
If online payment provides the highest direct benefit to customers and the business, while a color theme enhancement provides less value, the payment feature should be prioritized first even if some other items are easier or less risky.

🔹 Exam Tips:
If the exam asks how to order the Product Backlog, think first about business value or product value.
If the question is about what the product owner should prioritize when capacity is constrained, the answer is often value.
If the question focuses on what threatens Sprint completion, the answer may relate to risk, but this question is about prioritization, not threats.
If the question mentions effort or estimates, do not be misled; estimation is not the same as prioritization.
If the question is phrased as What should the product owner maximize? the answer is likely value.

Communication planning overlaps with stakeholder identification, analysis, prioritization, and

the most important factor in engaging with stakeholders effectively. Planning communication for the
project entails considering the following:
▶ Who needs information?

▶ What is the best way to provide information?

▶ Who has the information needed?
